verdict: Keep mapped output stores as an optional experiment. Leave the retained constructor unchanged: the fixed request has no measurable improvement; changing inputs show a modest benefit.
scope: Output-only mapping replaces two captured D2H copies with one bit-preserving Triton store kernel. Input staging remains one packed DMA copy; model arithmetic, host preparation and formatting are unchanged.

isolated_confirmed_short_us.note: Native replay plus synchronization around I/O and a tiny dependency-control kernel. This is not full-model latency. CUDA-event diagnostics are not an exposed-latency bound.

rejected_variant: Mapped input plus mapped output was slower than DMA for the isolated short workload, despite lower CUDA-event timing. It was not taken to full inference.

development_history.initial_abort: A probe destroyed external streams before releasing all pinned views. Correcting destruction order fixed the abort. Original error excerpt is preserved; original source is explicitly reconstructed, not archived.
development_history.strengthened_validation: Earlier shared buffers allowed a previous DMA mode to hide a stale mapped operation. Fresh results poison host/device/output buffers before each mode and compare independent CPU bits. Historical reports remain unchanged.

cuda_reference.application: Use stream synchronization to order CPU/GPU accesses to mapped pinned memory; the existing native Session synchronizes before Python sees output.
